ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a large outer circle, and the gray part inside the circle is the shaded region. Inside the circle there are two white unshaded circles arranged vertically, and the two are tangent at a point T; the upper white circle is tangent to the outer circle at the top, and the lower white circle is tangent to the outer circle at the bottom. The horizontal line segment PQ passes through the tangency point T of the two white circles, and P and Q are the intersection points of this horizontal chord with the outer circle. Reasoning: Let the radius of the upper white circle be a, and the radius of the lower white circle be b. Since the vertical diameter of the outer circle is composed of the diameters of the two white circles, the radius of the outer circle is a+b. The shaded area equals the area of the outer circle minus the areas of the two white circles: π(a+b)^2 - πa^2 - πb^2 = 2πab. The problem gives the shaded area as 2π, so 2πab = 2π, obtaining ab = 1. Taking the center of the outer circle as the origin and the vertical direction as the y-axis, the vertical distance of the tangency point T relative to the center of the outer circle is b-a. PQ is the horizontal chord of the outer circle at height y=b-a, therefore PQ = 2√((a+b)^2 - (b-a)^2) = 2√(4ab) = 4√ab. Because ab=1, PQ=4.

method.method_draft: Let the tangency point of the two white circles be T. From the image, read that the two unshaded circles are vertically tangent to each other, the upper one is tangent to the outer circle at the top, the lower one is tangent to the outer circle at the bottom, and PQ is a horizontal chord of the outer circle passing through T. Let the upper and lower radii be a and b. The outer radius is then a+b, since the vertical diameter is made of the two inner-circle diameters. The shaded area is the outer circle area minus the two inner circle areas: π(a+b)^2−πa^2−πb^2=2πab. The text gives this shaded area as 2π, so ab=1. Now place coordinates with the outer circle center on the vertical line through T. The vertical offset of T from the outer center is b−a, so the horizontal chord length is PQ=2√((a+b)^2−(b−a)^2)=4√ab=4.

From the diagram, draw the vertical diameter AB of the outer circle through the top and bottom tangency points; T lies on this diameter, and PQ is the horizontal chord through T.
